title: Check your fridge: Taylor Farms recalls H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit over undeclared soy and almonds
excerpt: Taylor Farms of Dallas is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit sold in Texas because it may contain undeclared soy and almonds, per an Oct. 27 FDA notice.
content:
Taylor Farms of Dallas is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit sold at H-E-B stores in Texas because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts (almonds), according to an Oct. 27 notice from the Food and Drug Administration and an H-E-B newsroom announcement the same day.

People who have a sensitivity or allergy to soy or almonds may be at risk of a serious or life-threatening allergic reaction if they eat the product, the FDA notice said. No adverse reactions had been reported as of Oct. 27.

How to identify the recalled kit

The recalled product is the H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit, 13.4 ounces, packaged in a plastic bag and distributed to H-E-B stores in Texas. Check the back of the package for these identifiers:

  • Best If Used By date: Oct. 30, 2026
  • UPC: 041220300457

Customers who bought the kit should not eat it. The recalled kits should be thrown away or returned to the store for a full refund, according to H-E-B and the FDA notice. Customers with questions may contact Taylor Farms at (855) 455-0098, Monday through Friday between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Pacific time.

Not the summer outbreak

This recall is a labeling issue, not a contamination finding, and it is not related to cyclospora or to Taylor Farms de Mexico, USA Today reported. Earlier this year, health officials identified iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms de Mexico as the source of a large cyclospora outbreak, and the FDA declared that outbreak over in September after concluding its investigation.

The distinction matters for shoppers in Laredo, where H-E-B is a routine stop and salad kits are a quick dinner option. An undeclared allergen recall does not mean every salad kit on the shelf is affected: only the specific H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit with the UPC and best-by date above is covered by this recall, and no other Taylor Farms salad kits were included at the time of the announcement.

Shoppers with a soy or almond allergy should check the back of the bag before serving, even if the kit was bought earlier in the week. If the UPC and date match, do not eat it.
